text:
Lin: quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC — ran into a couple of edge cases when enabling fused QKV + bias/rope with the dropout-free path. want opinions on fallback semantics and operator contract changes. TL;DR: correctness is fine, but perf/memory regressions at extreme seq-len and mixed-precision combos.

Alex: can you list the exact combos that regressed? is it only when rope is fused AND bias is applied, or does fused-qkv alone trigger it?

Lin: fused-qkv alone is ok for most models. issues show up when: (1) fuse_bias_rope=true && dropout=0.0 && use_fp16 && seq_len >= 4096, and (2) cross-attn with variable kv cache chunking. memory spikes and occasional NaNs.

Maya: hmm, NaNs + fp16 usually means a numeric accumulation path changed. did you observe any difference between continuous batching vs per-request execution?

Lin: yes — continuous batching exposes it more (higher mem pressure + larger effective matmul sizes). per-request single-shot runs are mostly fine.

Samir: i hit something similar last week with the cache layout change. quick thought: when we fuse qkv+bias+rope we pack tensors into a single buffer to avoid copies. that packing can change alignment/prefetch behavior on A100 and cause OOM-ish peaks for long sequences.

Alex: option A: keep operator contract identical (same input tensors) and make fused execution an internal strategy that falls back to unfused on memory-pressure or when accumulation risky. Option B: expose a new op variant with different inputs so we can explicitly opt-in and verify correctness per-model. pros/cons?

Maya: i prefer A for API stability. but we need a robust signal to decide fallback cheaply. maybe a runtime hint: exec_attrs { allow_fused_qkv: true, max_seq_for_fusion: 4096 }

Lin: i prototyped a simple threshold + trial-run: if seq_len > threshold we run a cheap preflight check (small GEMM) to test fp16 accumulation. overhead ~0.2ms per new seq-len bucket. seems acceptable.

Chris: for rollouts we should add canary metrics: token-error-rate, per-token-loss drift, mem-peak-percentile (P99), and kernel-fallback-rate. auto-fallback should be toggleable per-customer in Dedicated.

Samir: also add a debug dump for the packing offsets (only when debug env var enabled) so we can repro OOM on long sequences without full trace logs. short dump size ~ few KB.

Alex: implementation nit: keep a single op name FusedAttention but add an ExecHints proto (string map) instead of changing kernel signature. that keeps SPMD and JIT caches intact.

Lin: agreed. plan: 1) Node change: accept exec_hints map. 2) Runtime: implement threshold + quick-accumulation check. 3) Canary: enable for a small % of traffic with metrics Chris listed. 4) Fallback: unfused path when check fails or mem pressure high.

Maya: one more — tests. add a parametric test that runs combinations: {fp16,fp32} x {dropout=0,dropout=0.1} x {rope_fused, rope_unfused} x seq_len in {512,2048,8192}. CI should run minimal set on GPU and full set nightly on a cheaper CI pool.

Lin: i'll open an RFC follow-up doc with the exec_hints proto and the trial-run microbenchmark numbers. also adding the packing-offset debug dump.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: ref=fused-attn-fallbacks/2026-03-20, target=canary-5pct, started_by=Lin

Chris: thanks — once the RFC follow-up is up i'll review and propose the exact metric definitions for the console dashboards (:eyes:).

Samir: noted — ping me on the perf traces. i can help synthesize a seq-len stress test harness.

Alex: ok team — sounds like a good path forward. keep fused as a runtime strategy with safe fallbacks and explicit telemetry. :thumbsup:
